questions.q: A monochromatic light wave with wavelength& ${λ}_{1}$~and frequency~${ν}_{1}$~in air enters another medium. If the angle of incidence and angle of refraction at the interface are $45 °$ and $30 °$ respectively, then the wavelength~${λ}_{2}$~and frequency~${ν}_{2}$& of the refracted wave are:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
By using Snell's law,& ${n}_{1}sin{θ}_{1} = {n}_{2}sin{θ}_{2}$, the refractive index is~

$\mu = \dfrac{\sin 45 °}{\sin 30 °} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}}{\dfrac{1}{2}} = \sqrt{2}$

Also using the relation~$n = \dfrac{c}{v}$~where~$n$~is the refractive index,~$c$~is the velocity of light in air~and~$v$~is the velocity in the medium

$⇒ \dfrac{c\text{air}}{\text{v}} = \sqrt{2} = \dfrac{\lambda\text{1}}{\lambda2}$

The velocities~are~given by~

$v = ν{λ}_{2}c = ν{λ}_{1}$

$⇒ {λ}_{1} = \sqrt{2}{λ}_{2}$~and~${ν}_{1} = {ν}_{2}$.

The frequency of light does not change when the medium changes.

questions.q: When an object is placed 40 cm away from a spherical mirror an image of magnification $\frac{1}{2}$ is produced. To obtain an image with magnification of $\frac{1}{3}$, the object is to be moved :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{m}=\frac{1}{2}=\frac{\mathrm{f}}{\mathrm{f}-\mathrm{u}} \\ & \frac{1}{2}=\frac{\mathrm{f}}{\mathrm{f}-(-40)} \\ & \mathrm{f}+40=2 \mathrm{f} \Rightarrow \mathrm{f}=40 \mathrm{~cm} \\ & \text { now } \mathrm{m}=\frac{1}{3}=\frac{40}{40-\mathrm{u}} \\ & 40-\mathrm{u}=120 \Rightarrow \mathrm{u}=-80\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A convex lens of focal length $20$ cm produces images of the same magnification 2 when an object is kept at two distances ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}  \left({x}_{1}> {x}_{2}\right)$ from the lens. The ratio of ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2} is:$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given, \left|m\right| = 2 ⇒ m = \pm 2$
From this lens formula, $\dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$
$\dfrac{u}{v} + 1 = \dfrac{u}{f}$
$\dfrac{1}{m} + 1 = \dfrac{u}{f}$
$u = f \left(\dfrac{1}{m} +1\right)$
${x}_{1} = 20 \left(1 + $\dfrac{1}{2}\right)
${x}_{2} = 20 \left($1 - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)
\dfrac{{x}_{1}}{{x}_{2}} = \dfrac{3}{1}$

questions.q: The critical angle for a denser-rarer interface is $45 °$.~The speed of light in rarer medium is $3 \times {10}^{8}ms^{- 1}$. The speed of light in the denser medium is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The critical angle and the refractive index of a media are related by the formula:

$sin{θ}_{c} = \left(\dfrac{1}{μ}\right) . . .\left(1\right)$

Substitute the value of the critical angle into equation (1) and solve to calculate the refractive index of the medium.

$\begin{cases}\sin 45 ° & = & \dfrac{1}{μ}\\ ⇒ & \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{1}{μ}\\ ⇒ & \mu = \sqrt{2}\end{cases}$

The refractive index of the medium can also be written as

$\mu = \dfrac{c}{v} . . . \left($2\right)$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (2) and solve to calculate the required speed of light within the medium.

$\begin{cases}\sqrt{2} \text{ and } = \text{ and } \dfrac{3 \times {10}^{8}ms^{- 1}}{v}\\ ⇒ \text{ and } v = \dfrac{3 \times {10}^{8}ms^{- 1}}{2}\\ = \text{ and } 2 . 12 \times {10}^{8}ms^{- 1}\end{cases}$

$

questions.q: The power of a lens (biconvex) is $1 . 25m^{- 1}$ in particular medium. Refractive index of the lens is $1 . 5$~and radii of curvature are $20$ cm and $40$ cm respectively. The refractive index of surrounding medium:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using Len's maker formula,

$P = \dfrac{1}{f} = \left({μ}_{1} - {μ}_{2}\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{R1} - \dfrac{1}{R2}\right)~

Where,~${μ}_{1}$ is refractive index of lens and ${μ}_{2}$ is of surrounding medium.~

Putting the values,~

$⇒ 1 . 25 = \left($1 . 5 - {μ}_{2}\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{0 . 2} + \dfrac{1}{0 . 4}\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{1 . 25 \times 0 . 08}{0 . 6} = \left(1 . 5 - {μ}_{2}\right)$

The refractive index of surrounding medium is~${μ}_{2} = \dfrac{4}{3}.$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R

Assertion A: The phase difference of two light waves change if they travel through different media having same thickness, but different indices of& refraction.

Reason R: The wavelengths of waves are different in different media.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is not correct but R is correct
A is correct but R is not correct
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When light travels through a medium, its velocity depends on the density of the medium.

The formula to calculate the speed of light can be written as

$v = ν\lambda . . . ( 1 )$

From equation (1), it can be concluded that higher the speed, higher is the wavelength. Hence, the wavelength of light depends on the refractive index of the medium.

Because of changed wavelength the phase difference changes while the two waves travel the same distance.

Thus, both& A& and& R& are correct and& R& is the correct explanation of& A.

questions.q: Given a thin convex lens (refractive index $\mu_2$ ), kept in a liquid (refractive index $\mu_1, \mu_1 \lt \mu_2$ ) having radii of curvatures \left|R_1\right|$ and \left|R_2\right|$. Its second surface is silver polished. Where should an object be placed on the optic axis so that a real and inverted image is formed at the same place?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{eq}}}=\frac{2}{\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{L}}}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{m}}} \\ & \mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{m}}=-\frac{\left|\mathrm{R}_2\right|}{2} \\ & \frac{1}{\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{L}}}=\left(\frac{\mu_2}{\mu_1}-1\right)\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}_1}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}_2}\right)\end{aligned}$\begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{eq}}}=2\left(\frac{\mu_2-\mu_1}{\mu_1}\right)\left(\frac{\mathrm{R}_1+\mathrm{R}_2}{\mathrm{R}_1 \mathrm{R}_2}\right)+\frac{2}{\mathrm{R}_2} \\ & =\frac{2}{\mathrm{R}_2}\left[\frac{\left(\mu_2-\mu_1\right)\left(\mathrm{R}_1+\mathrm{R}_2\right)+\mu_1 \mathrm{R}_1}{\mu_1 \mathrm{R}_1}\right] \\ & =\frac{2}{\mathrm{R}_2}\left[\frac{\mu_2 \mathrm{R}_1+\mu_2 \mathrm{R}_2-\mu_1 \mathrm{R}_1-\mu_1 \mathrm{R}_2+\mu_1 \mathrm{R}_1}{\mu_1 \mathrm{R}_1}\right] \\ & \frac{1}{\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{eq}}}=\frac{2\left[\mu_2 \mathrm{R}_1+\mu_2 \mathrm{R}_2-\mu_1 \mathrm{R}_2\right]}{\mu_1 \mathrm{R}_1 \mathrm{R}_2} \end{aligned}$$ For same size of image $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{u}=2 \mathrm{f} \\ & \mathrm{u}=\frac{\mu_1 \mathrm{R}_1 \mathrm{R}_2}{\mu_2 \mathrm{R}_1+\mu_2 \mathrm{R}_2-\mu_1 \mathrm{R}_2} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: An object is at a distance of $20 \mathrm{~m}$ from a convex lens of focal length $0.3 \mathrm{~m}$. The lens forms an image of the object. If the object moves away from the lens at a speed of $5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ the speed and direction of the image will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Bylens formula $\begin{array}{l} \frac{1}{v}-\frac{1}{u}=\frac{1}{f}\\ \frac{1}{v}-\frac{1}{(-20)}=\frac{10}{3}\\ \frac{1}{v}=\frac{10}{3}-\frac{1}{20}\\ \frac{1}{v}=\frac{197}{60}; \quad v=\frac{60}{197} \end{array} Magnification of lens (m) is given by \mathrm{m}=\left(\frac{\mathrm{v}}{\mathrm{u}}\right)=\frac{\left(\frac{60}{197}\right)}{20} velocity of image wrt. to lens is given by \mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{J} / \mathrm{L}}=\mathrmm^{2} \mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{O} / \mathrm{L}} direction of velocity of image is same as that of object $\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{O} / \mathrm{L}}=5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s} \\ \mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{I} / \mathrm{L}}=\left(\frac{60 \times 1}{197 \times 20}\right)^{2} \end{array}$=1.16 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ towards the lens

questions.q: A convex lens of focal length 30 cm is placed in contact with a concave lens of focal length 20 cm. An object is placed at 20 cm to the left of this lens system. The distance of the image from the lens in cm is ________
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Equivalent focal length
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{1}{f}=\frac{1}{f_1}+\frac{1}{f_2} \\ & =\frac{1}{30}+\frac{1}{-20}=\frac{2-3}{60}=-\frac{1}{60} \\ & f=-60 \mathrm{~cm}
\end{aligned}$
Lens formula
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{1}{\mathrm{v}}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{u}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}} \\ & \frac{1}{\mathrm{v}}-\frac{1}{-20}=\frac{1}{-60} \\ & \mathrm{v}=-15 \mathrm{~cm}
\end{aligned}$

Now a glass block (refractive index 1.5)$ of 1.5$ cm thickness is placed in between the light source and the lens. To get the sharp image again, the screen is shifted by a distance $d .$ Then $d$ is:

questions.solution:
From given data

$\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$

$\dfrac{1}{10} - \dfrac{1}{( - 10 )} = \dfrac{1}{f}$

$f = 5cm$

When glass plate is placed, shift in object for lens

$s = t \left(1 - \dfrac{1}{\mu}\right) =1.5 \left($1 - $\dfrac{2}{3}\right)

$= 0.5cm$

Shift will be in the direction of incoming rays

$∴ u = 10 - 0.5 = 9.5cm$

\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}

\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{5} + \dfrac{1}{( - 9.5 )}

$v = $\dfrac{47.5}{4.5}$cm$

Shift =\dfrac{47.5}{4.5} -$10 = $\dfrac{2.5}{4.5} = \dfrac{5}{9}$cm = 0.55cm$ away from lens.$

questions.q: When a beam of white light is allowed to pass through convex lens parallel to principal axis, the different colours of light converge at different point on the principle axis after refraction. This is called :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Due to difference in refractive index of a material for different wavelengths, the focal length will be different for different colours. This will cause a separation of parallel beam of white light. This phenomenon is known as chromatic aberration.

Polarisation& is a property applying to transverse waves that specify the geometrical orientation of the oscillations.

When energy waves (such as light, sound, and various electromagnetic waves) are caused to depart from a straight path due to imperfections in the medium it is called Scattering.

Spherical aberration is present when the outer parts of a lens do not bring light rays into the same focus as the central part.&

questions.q: A $2$~meter long scale with least count of $0 . 2cm$ is used to measure the locations of objects on an optical bench. While measuring the focal length of~a convex lens, the object pin and the convex lens are placed at $80$ cm mark and $1m$ mark, respectively. The image of the object pin on the other side of lens coincides with image pin that is kept at $180$ cm mark. The $%$ error in the estimation of focal length is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula for a lens is given by& $\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} . . . ( i )$

$u = \left(100 \pm 0 . 2\right)cm - \left(80 \pm 0 . 2\right)cm = \left(20 \pm 0 . 4\right)cm$

$v = \left(180 \pm 0 . 2\right)cm - \left(100 \pm 0 . 2\right)cm = \left(80 \pm 0 . 4\right)cm$

Substituting the~values in the equation of focal length,

$\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{80} - \left(- \dfrac{1}{20}\right) = \dfrac{5}{80}$

$⇒ f = 16cm$

Differentiating the equation (i)

$\dfrac{df}{f2} = \dfrac{dv}{v2} + \dfrac{du}{u2}$(Only positive sign is considered for~error calculation)

$= \dfrac{0 . 4}{6400} + \dfrac{0 . 4}{400} = 0 . 4 \times \dfrac{17}{6400}$

$⇒ df = 0 . 4 \times \dfrac{17}{6400} \times {16}^{2} = 0 . 272$

The percentage error is~

$\dfrac{df}{f} \times 100 = \dfrac{0 . 272}{16} \times 100 = 1 . 70 %$

questions.q: The refractive index of a transparent liquid filled in an equilateral hollow prism is $\sqrt{2}$. The angle of minimum deviation for the liquid will be _______°.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For minimum deviation in a prism,

$\mu = \dfrac{\sin \left(\dfrac{{D}_\min + A}{2}\right)}{sin\dfrac{A}{2}}$

The value of minimum deviation is

$⇒ \sqrt{2} = \dfrac{\sin \left(\dfrac{{D}_\min + 60 °}{2}\right)}{\sin 30 °}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2} = \sin \left(\dfrac{{D}_\min + 60 °}{2}\right) ⇒ 45 ° = \left(\dfrac{{D}_\min + 60 °}{2}\right) ⇒ {D}_\min = 30 °$

When the refracted light just grazes the boundary& the incident& angle is called a critical angle.

Using snell's law at face $AC$.

$1 . 5\sin 60 ° = n \times \sin 90 °$~

$⇒ 1 . 5 \times \dfrac{3}{2} = n = \dfrac{x}{4}$~

$⇒ 3\sqrt{3} = \sqrt{x}$

$⇒ x = 27$
